questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Magnesium skarn deposits, formed by the interaction of granitic intrusions with dolomite, contain which minerals?
options: Mg-Ti-Fe skarn from dolomite + granitic intrusions. Phlogopite, forsterite, spinel
VMS deposits formed by submarine volcanic exhalation of metal-rich brines
Porphyry copper deposits characterized by concentric alteration halos and abundant stockwork veining
Calcic skarn developed from limestone with garnet, pyroxene and wollastonite
questions.solution: Skarn: Ca (calcic) or Mg (magnesian). W, Cu, Fe, Zn. Pyroxene + garnet + wollastonite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In potassium-argon radiometric dating, obtaining a reliable age requires the measurement of which quantities?
options: Measurement of K and Ar independently
Only measurement of the potassium content alone
Only measurement of the trapped argon content alone
Both the daughter isotopes of the same element
questions.solution: K-Ar: 40K → 40Ar. Measure K by flame photometry/ICP, Ar by mass spectrometry. Ar must be trapped (closure temperature).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What do load casts on the base of a sedimentary bed indicate about their formation?
options: Ridge-like projections found on the top surface of the sandstone bed
Irregular pods confined to the interior of a single thick massive bed
Bulbous projections on bottom of bed. Soft sediment deformation
Straight, parallel ridges aligned exactly with the bedding plane direction
questions.solution: Load cast: differential loading. Flute cast: current scour. Both sole marks (bottom of bed).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Kink band, a narrow zone in which foliation abruptly changes orientation, indicates which deformation mechanism?
options: Shear along discrete planes
Homogeneous pure shear at high strain rate
Layer-parallel extension in a rift basin
Lithostatic loading under hydrostatic stress
questions.solution: Kink band: sharp fold with straight limbs. Indicates simple shear. Common in foliated rocks with strong planar fabric.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which ultrapotassic, mantle-derived rock is diamond-bearing, as at Argyle, Australia?
options: Granitic rock rich in quartz and muscovite of typical continental crust
Andesitic volcanic rock intermediate between basalt and rhyolite
Basaltic rock of tholeiitic affinity erupted at mid-ocean ridges
Ultrapotassic mantle-derived. Diamond-bearing (Argyle, Australia)
questions.solution: Lamproite: K-rich, Mg-rich. Phlogopite + olivine + K-richerite. Source rock for diamonds.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A symplectite is best described as what type of texture in metamorphic rocks?
options: Regular growth of a single mineral phase in optical continuity across a twin plane with no second phase present
Overgrowth of a new mineral in crystallographic continuity around an older detrital or igneous core
Intergrowth of two minerals (e.g., Cpx + Pl) replacing higher-P assemblage. Opx + Cpx + Pl from Grt breakdown
Exsolution of a second mineral phase from a homogeneous alkali-feldspar host during slow cooling
questions.solution: Symplectite: vermicular texture. Decompression reaction. Fingerprint of rapid exhumation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In GIS, the raster data model represents continuous data such as elevation using what arrangement of grid cells?
options: Points, lines and polygons, with topological relationships that are shared between the features
Vector data structures, with precise shared boundary topology between the map features
Discrete polygons only, with no support for representing continuous surfaces at all
Grid cells. Continuous data (elevation, rainfall). Cell size = resolution
questions.solution: Raster: simple analysis, large storage. Compression: run-length, LZW, JPEG2000.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A condensed section, deposited slowly during maximum flooding, is characterized by what, and what kind of surface does it form?
options: Slow deposition (pelagic/hemipelagic) during maximum flooding. High organic matter. Downlap surface
Rapid deposition of coarse clastic sediments during forced regression when the entire shelf is exposed and eroded
Formation during lowstand when the shelf is exposed and eroded
Coarse-grained lag deposits formed during early transgressive reworking
questions.solution: Condensed: glauconite, phosphorite, organic-rich. Maximum flooding surface (MFS).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which property of mica is well known for causing it to split into thin flexible sheets?
options: Basal cleavage (it splits into thin sheets)
Cubic cleavage producing right-angled fragments
Conchoidal fracture resembling broken glass surfaces
Rhombic cleavage developed in three directions
questions.solution: Mica has one perfect cleavage direction, peeling into thin elastic sheets.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A volcanic rock containing many gas-bubble cavities is described as:
options: Phaneritic
Foliated
Porphyritic
Vesicular
questions.solution: Vesicles are voids left by escaping gas in rapidly cooled lava (e.g. scoria, pumice).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The coal rank with the highest fixed-carbon content and calorific value is:
options: Anthracite
Lignite
Bituminous
Peat
questions.solution: Anthracite is the highest-rank coal, with the greatest carbon content and heating value.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a rift zone, extension and thinning of continental lithosphere during continental rifting ultimately leads to which outcome?
options: Formation of a new subduction zone within the continental interior
Uplift and erosion of the rift flanks without any thinning of the crust
Passive margin (if successful) or failed rift (aulacogen)
Instant splitting of the continent into two separate microplates
questions.solution: Rift: East African (active), Atlantic (passive margins). Aulacogen: failed arm of triple junction.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Plate motion, ultimately powered by mantle convection, is driven most strongly by which force?
options: Slab pull — the gravitational pull of the dense, subducting slab
Basal drag exerted by convection currents on the base of the plate
Momentum imparted by deep mantle plumes rising beneath the plate
Tidal attraction of the Moon and Sun acting on the crust
questions.solution: Slab pull — the gravitational pull of the dense, subducting slab

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The five major Phanerozoic mass extinction events occurred at the end of which periods?
options: A single major event at the end of the Precambrian that removed all shelly faunas
Ordovician, Devonian, Permian, Triassic, Cretaceous
Only two events: the end-Cretaceous asteroid impact and the mid-Pleistocene ice ages
No recognisable pattern, with extinction pulses scattered randomly through every period
questions.solution: P-T extinction: 95% marine species. K-Pg: dinosaurs. End-Ordovician: glaciation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The supercontinent Pangaea was in existence during which geological time span?
options: Late Paleozoic to Early Mesozoic
Early Paleozoic following the Cambrian explosion
Mid-Cretaceous peak of seafloor spreading
Cenozoic assembly through the Alpine-Himalayan orogeny
questions.solution: Pangaea: assembled Carboniferous-Permian, broke up Jurassic-Cretaceous. Caused significant climate and biogeographic effects.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Lateritic bauxite, a residual deposit, consists chiefly of which aluminum hydroxide minerals?
options: Primary igneous crystallization of aluminum oxide minerals directly from a cooling basaltic magma chamber in the crust
Al(OH)₃ (gibbsite, boehmite, diaspore). Intense lateritic weathering of aluminosilicate rocks
Hydrothermal precipitation of aluminum hydroxide from hot chloride brines
Metamorphic recrystallization of aluminous pelites into corundum schists
questions.solution: Bauxite: Al ore. Weipa (Australia), Panchpatmali (India). Laterite caps.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On a concordia diagram used in U-Pb geochronology, data points that plot below the concordia curve indicate what?
options: Discordance from lead loss
The age of the sample plotted at one point
The chemical composition of the uranium minerals
The pressure conditions of crystallization alone
questions.solution: Concordia: 206Pb/238U vs 207Pb/235U. Discordant points indicate lead loss. Upper intercept = crystallization age.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Metamorphic reaction textures: coronas (symplectites):
options: Random intergrowth of minerals formed by complete recrystallization of the rock
Crystal faces that grow freely into an open fluid-filled cavity
Layering inherited directly from the original sedimentary bedding
Rim minerals around reactant mineral, formed during incomplete reaction
questions.solution: Corona: olivine rimmed by Opx+Spinel. Symplectite: vermicular intergrowth. Records reaction progress.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Metamorphism at chlorite grade is indicative of which metamorphic facies?
options: Low-grade greenschist facies
Granulite facies high-temperature metamorphism
Zeolite facies very shallow burial conditions
Blueschist facies high-pressure metamorphism
questions.solution: Chlorite: index mineral for greenschist facies. ~300-450°C, moderate pressure. Typical of regional metamorphism.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What process and climatic conditions lead to the formation of laterite and bauxite?
options: Dry climate with intense mechanical weathering and no chemical alteration
Periglacial freeze-thaw cycles producing frost-shattered angular debris
Intense chemical weathering under tropical monsoon. Fe/Al enrichment. Bauxite
Cold climate with glacial grinding and slow chemical weathering of the bedrock
questions.solution: Laterite: duricrust. Age: Tertiary-Quaternary. Transition: laterite → bauxite (Al-rich).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a desert region, a bajada is best described as what kind of landform?
options: Coalescing alluvial fans at mountain base
An isolated conical alluvial fan deposit
A river terrace abandoned by channel incision
A wave-built terrace along a retreating coast
questions.solution: Bajada: series of overlapping alluvial fans forming apron at mountain front. Common in arid regions.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the correct sequence of stages in a site investigation?
options: Drilling is always carried out before any desk study or field mapping is done
Desk study → field mapping → geophysics → drilling → in-situ testing
Only in-situ testing of the surface without any drilling or coring
Geophysics alone, followed directly by construction without borings
questions.solution: Phased approach: each stage informs next. Minimize cost, maximize information.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Quartz c-axis preferred orientation in deformed rocks is produced mainly by which process?
options: Random crystallographic orientation that is completely unaffected by deformation, temperature or recrystallization
Only planar fabrics are produced, with no preferred c-axis orientation
No crystallographic fabric develops because quartz never deforms by slip
Crystallographic fabric by dynamic recrystallization. Type I (basal slip) vs Type II (prism slip) cross-girdles
questions.solution: Quartz CPO: fabric temperature-dependent. Low T: basal <a>. High T: prism <a>.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Graptolites are index fossils for the Ordovician-Silurian interval; their two major groups, dendroid and graptoloid, differ in what?
options: Permian. Benthic colonial bryozoans. Fenestrate and cryptostome forms together dominate the standard zonation
Ordovician-Silurian. Planktonic colonial hemichordates. Dendroid (benthic) vs graptoloid (planktonic)
Devonian-Mississippian. Solitary rugose corals. Zonation rests on dissepiment structure
Cambrian-Ordovician. Benthic archaeocyaths. Zonation is built on cone wall porosity
questions.solution: Graptolites: organic (periderm). Didymograptus (L. Ordovician), Monograptus (Silurian). Extinct Devonian.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What are the units and basis of classification used in the discipline of chronostratigraphy?
options: Time-rock units (System, Series, Stage). Based on absolute or relative age
Fossil-based correlation using the first and last appearance of index taxa
Rock type classification based purely on mineral composition and texture
Magnetic polarity reversal patterns calibrated against the geomagnetic time scale
questions.solution: Chronostratigraphic: Cretaceous System, Oxfordian Stage. Geochronologic: Cretaceous Period.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Freeze-thaw, exfoliation and salt crystal growth are physical processes, whereas dissolution, oxidation and hydrolysis belong to which class?
options: Weathering consists only of frost action acting on exposed rock surfaces in the cold climatic regions of the world today
Weathering consists only of the hydrolysis of silicate minerals taking place within the soil as the sole chemical weathering process in operation
Weathering consists only of the mechanical wedging of rock by plant roots growing in the cracks of the rock
Physical (freeze-thaw, exfoliation, salt crystal growth) and chemical (dissolution, oxidation, hydrolysis)
questions.solution: Physical: mechanical breakup. Chemical: mineral alteration. Spheroidal weathering of jointed rock.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is stereographic projection primarily used for in the analysis of structural geology data?
options: A type of geological map projection used to preserve areas of land mass
A two-dimensional block diagram showing the three-dimensional geometry of folds
A cross-section drawn perpendicular to the strike of the fold axial plane
Tool for structural data analysis (poles to planes, fold axes)
questions.solution: Stereonet: lower hemisphere equal-area (Schmidt) or equal-angle (Wulff).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Electrical conductivity in the mantle increases with depth, and the asthenosphere shows higher conductivity because of what?
options: Zero. The mantle is a perfect insulator at all depths and temperatures
Increases with depth. Asthenosphere: higher conductivity (partial melt)
Decreases with depth. The asthenosphere is the least conductive layer beneath the lithosphere
Same throughout. Conductivity is constant from the Moho to the core-mantle boundary
questions.solution: Mantle conductivity: olivine + melt. High conductivity zone: asthenosphere. MT imaging.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the induced polarization (IP) method, the measured chargeability is especially useful for detecting which type of subsurface material?
options: Chargeability (mV/V). Sulfide mineral detection. Time-domain (decay curve) and frequency-domain
Measures the magnetic susceptibility contrast to locate disseminated magnetite bodies in the bedrock
Uses P- and S-wave travel times to delineate low velocity zones within sedimentary basins
Profiles the residual gravity field to detect buried cavities and voids in karst terrain
questions.solution: IP: metallic mineralization. Disseminated sulfides. Polarization effect at grain-fluid interface.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How do granite and granodiorite differ in their feldspar proportions?
options: Both rocks have identical feldspar ratios and differ only in grain size
Granodiorite contains feldspathoids while granite contains no feldspathoids
Granite: K-feldspar > Plagioclase. Granodiorite: Plagioclase > K-feldspar
The two rocks cannot be distinguished by their modal mineral proportions
questions.solution: QAPF diagram: Granite = Q + A > P. Granodiorite = Q + P > A.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Fluvial terrace classification: strath vs fill:
options: Both strath and fill terraces are cut entirely into the underlying bedrock of the river valley during the process of incision
Both strath and fill terraces are built entirely of alluvial sediment deposits that were laid down by the river at some earlier stage
Strath and fill terraces are identical in every respect and cannot be distinguished in the field by any method at all
Strath: bedrock surface cut during incision. Fill: alluvial deposit abandoned during incision
questions.solution: Strath: planation surface. Fill: alluvial remnant. Strath = bedrock. Fill = alluvium.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the repeating structural unit of the double chain in amphibole silicates?
options: Si₂O₇ isolated double tetrahedra sharing one apex only
Si₄O₁₁⁶⁻ repeating unit. Two pyroxene chains linked
Si₄O₁₀ single rings of four linked tetrahedra
SiO₄ independent tetrahedra isolated from each other
questions.solution: Amphibole: double chain inosilicate. Perfect 56°/124° cleavage. OH in structure.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock sample of 100 cm³ contains 25 cm³ of pore space. Its porosity is:
questions.solution: Porosity = (void volume/total volume)×100 = 25/100 = 25%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquiclude is a saturated geological unit that is essentially impermeable and yields no significant water; it is typically composed of:
options: Impermeable unit (clay, massive shale). No significant yield
A saturated permeable unit that yields useful quantities of water
A fractured rock unit with good storage and moderate transmission
A coarse sand bed that transmits water with very little resistance
questions.solution: Aquiclude: prevents flow. Confining layer in confined aquifer.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The hydraulic conductivity K of a porous medium depends on the medium and the fluid; for sands it typically ranges:
options: Depends only on the porosity of the rock medium being considered
Depends on medium + fluid. Sand: 10⁻²-10⁻⁴ m/s. Clay: <10⁻⁹ m/s
Is a property of the rock alone and not of the fluid moving through it
Is constant for all geological materials at any temperature
questions.solution: K: gravel (10⁻¹), sand (10⁻³), silt (10⁻⁵), clay (10⁻⁸ m/s). K = m/s or m/day.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Pumping from a well creates a cone of depression in the water table; the extent of this cone is described by its:
options: Drawdown cone around pumping well. Radius of influence R
A flat horizontal water surface that is unaffected by the pump
A mound of water that builds up above the pumping well
An inverted cone representing the rise of water near the well
questions.solution: Drawdown: s₀ = Q/(2πT)·ln(R/r_w). R increases with pumping time.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a pumping test, the specific capacity of a well is defined as the discharge per unit drawdown, and it is expressed as:
options: Q×s₀ with s₀ measured at the end of the pumping test period
s₀/Q giving the ratio of drawdown to the pumping rate applied to the well
Q/s₀ = 2πT/ln(R/r_w). Q=displacement rate, s₀=drawdown at well
1/Q evaluated at a fixed drawdown value for the well under test conditions
questions.solution: Specific capacity: Q/s₀. Indicates well productivity. Affected by well efficiency.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The accessory mineral zircon crystallizes in which crystal system?
options: Orthorhombic
Hexagonal
Cubic
Tetragonal
questions.solution: Zircon (ZrSiO4) — tetragonal prisms. High RI, high birefringence. Used in U-Pb dating.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes pingos, their morphology and the two systems by which they form?
options: Cone-shaped hill built up by repeated eruptions of lava and pyroclastic material around a central volcanic vent
Ridge of wind-blown sand aligned with the prevailing wind direction in a desert region
Ice-cored mounds in permafrost. Open-system (groundwater) and closed-system (lake)
Ridge of unsorted debris deposited along the margin of a glacier during a period of retreat
questions.solution: Pingo: up to 100m high. Collapse pingo → thermokarst pond. Continuous permafrost zone.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index):
options: (NIR-Red)/(NIR+Red). Values -1 to 1. Healthy vegetation > 0.5
(Red-NIR)/(Red+NIR), which is positive for healthy vegetation
Simple NIR/Red ratio ranging between 0 and 1 for all surfaces
(NIR+Red)/NIR ratio, high values for bare soil surfaces
questions.solution: NDVI: >0.5 = dense vegetation. 0-0.2 = sparse. <0 = water/bare soil.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In cut slope design, which condition leads to plane failure?
options: Slope design ignores the orientation of bedding and joints entirely
Slope angle alone, with no consideration of rock mass structure
Only the height of the slope controls the stability of the cut
Dip slope vs anti-dip slope. Daylighting of bedding → plane failure
questions.solution: Daylighting: bedding dips out of slope → sliding. Rock bolts, drainage, berms.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the intermediate plutonic rock composed of plagioclase and hornblende?
options: Ultramafic plutonic rock composed almost entirely of olivine and pyroxene
Felsic plutonic rock dominated by quartz, alkali feldspar and muscovite
Mafic plutonic rock consisting of calcic plagioclase, augite and olivine
Intermediate plutonic (plagioclase + hornblende)
questions.solution: Diorite: no quartz or minor quartz. More plagioclase than K-spar.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On what basis are rocks classified and zoned in the discipline of biostratigraphy?
options: Based on fossil content (biozone, assemblage zone, range zone)
Based on the magnetic polarity of the rocks and reversal sequences
Based on the lithological character of the strata and their mineralogy
Based on radioactive decay of isotopes to give absolute ages in years
questions.solution: Biozone: body fossil or trace fossil. Index fossils: ammonite zones for Mesozoic.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: According to the Wentworth scale, how are grain sizes from clay to gravel defined in sedimentary rocks?
options: Clay < 0.1 mm, Silt 0.1-1 mm, Sand 1-10 mm, Gravel > 10 mm
Clay < 1 mm, Silt 1-4 mm, Sand 4-16 mm, Gravel > 16 mm
Clay < 1/256 mm, Silt 1/256-1/16 mm, Sand 1/16-2 mm, Gravel > 2 mm
Clay < 1/64 mm, Silt 1/64-1/4 mm, Sand 1/4-4 mm, Gravel 4-64 mm, Cobble > 64 mm
questions.solution: Wentworth: clay, silt, sand, pebble, cobble, boulder. Phi scale = -log2(mm).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Metamorphic facies series: Barrovian type:
options: Low-pressure/high-temperature gradient typical of shallow contact metamorphism
Very high-pressure gradient producing blueschist and eclogite facies rocks
Medium P/T gradient (typical of continental collision). Kyanite → sillimanite
High-temperature/low-pressure gradient typical of magmatic arc and rift settings worldwide
questions.solution: Barrovian: clockwise P-T path. Kyanite → sillimanite. Buchan: andalusite → sillimanite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Electromagnetic induction logging, which requires no contact with the borehole wall, measures what property of the formation?
options: Spontaneous potential and gamma ray logs used for bed correlation in cased holes only
Laterolog resistivity that requires direct galvanic contact with the borehole fluid for the measurement
Neutron porosity from an isotopic source used for gas detection in uncased wells
Conductivity σ (mS/m). Low frequency, no borehole contact. Used in PVC-cased wells, freshwater
questions.solution: EM induction: no electrode contact. Air-filled boreholes. Freshwater vs saline aquifer.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A laterally extensive coal seam indicates which type of depositional environment?
options: Widespread swamp or peat-forming environment
A single local river channel cutting through marine strata
A deep anoxic ocean basin far from any terrestrial landmass
Rapid burial by a volcanic eruption under marine waters
questions.solution: Coal: formed in terrestrial swamps. Extent = stable peat-forming.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Sm-Nd depleted mantle model age (T_DM) represents the time when a sample had the same ¹⁴³Nd/¹⁴⁴Nd ratio as:
options: Time when sample had same ¹⁴³Nd/¹⁴⁴Nd as depleted mantle
Cooling age of the rock below its mineral blocking temperature
Formation age of the host sedimentary basin in which it occurs
Metamorphic age of the enclosing rock suite and its minerals
questions.solution: T_DM: crustal residence time. Depleted mantle: ¹⁴³Nd/¹⁴⁴Nd grows with time. Model age = when sample split.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed drops 10 m over a horizontal distance of 40 m. Its dip angle is about:
questions.solution: dip = tan⁻¹(rise/run) = tan⁻¹(10/40) ≈ 14°.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 10% moisture, 25% volatile matter and 20% ash. Its fixed carbon is:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The soil profile above the water table consists of which zones, from top to bottom?
options: Saturated zone, capillary fringe, vadose zone (unsaturated). Roots in vadose
Only the saturated zone that lies beneath the water table surface level
Only the vadose zone that lies between the land surface and the water table surface below
Only the capillary fringe that overlies the regional water table surface
questions.solution: Vadose zone: moisture content < porosity. Infiltration, evapotranspiration, interflow.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How do the minerals chlorite and biotite differ from each other in thin section?
options: Chlorite: anomalous interference colors. Biotite: strong pleochroism, bird's eye extinction
Both minerals appear absolutely identical in every optical property when studied under the microscope
Differentiation based only on refractive index measurement
Birefringence values alone distinguish the two minerals
questions.solution: Chlorite: lower birefringence, green/brown. Biotite: high birefringence, strong absorption.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How does a fill terrace, cut into alluvium, differ from a strath terrace cut into bedrock with thin alluvial cover?
options: Fill and strath terraces are the same type of feature with no difference
Both fill and strath terraces are always formed in alluvial deposits of the river
Fill: in alluvium. Strath: bedrock terrace with thin alluvial cover
Both fill and strath terraces are always cut directly into bedrock
questions.solution: Fill terrace: former floodplain now abandoned. Strath terrace: lateral planation surface.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which remote sensing technique records hundreds of narrow contiguous bands and enables mineral identification by spectral signatures?
options: A few broad bands only, which cannot resolve the narrow absorption features at all
A single panchromatic band, which offers a very high spatial resolution only
100s of narrow bands. Spectral signature identification of minerals
Broad multispectral bands, which are used only for general land cover mapping work
questions.solution: Hyperspectral: AVIRIS, Hyperion, PRISMA, EnMAP. Mineral mapping (clay, iron, carbonate).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Why is quick clay considered extremely hazardous when disturbed?
options: A stiff cemented clay that permanently gains strength when it is disturbed by any loading
Thixotropic clay (high sensitivity). If disturbed, loses strength → flow failure
A clay with sensitivity below 2 that is always fully stable and strong
A clay that cannot flow even under very high pore water pressure
questions.solution: Quick clay: marine clay, leached to low salinity. Sensitivity > 30. Liquefaction flow slides.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which ultramafic rock of olivine and pyroxene represents mantle composition?
options: Granitic plutonic rock rich in quartz, K-feldspar and biotite
Ultramafic rock (olivine + pyroxene). Mantle composition
Dioritic rock composed of plagioclase, hornblende and minor quartz
Syenitic rock consisting mainly of alkali feldspar with little quartz
questions.solution: Peridotite: >90% mafic minerals. Source rock for basaltic magmas.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which formal stratigraphic formations are recognised within the Deccan Traps sequence?
options: Single lava flow that erupted in one continuous event over the entire craton
Two formations separated by a single regional unconformity throughout the pile
Formations: Jawhar, Igatpuri, Neral, Thakurwadi, Bhimashankar, Khandala, etc.
Ten formations of equal thickness with identical geochemical signatures in all flows
questions.solution: Deccan: ~3500m thick in Western Ghats. Twelve formations in Wai Subgroup. Intertrappean beds.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the primary composition and origin of the sedimentary rock limestone?
options: CaCO3 (calcite) — biochemical or chemical
CaMg(CO3)2 — formed by replacement of limestone during diagenesis
SiO2 — chemical precipitate of silica in deep marine basins
Fe2O3 — iron oxide precipitated in oxidizing continental environments
questions.solution: Limestone: fossiliferous, chalk, coquina, oolitic. Effervesces in HCl.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Gneissic banding refers to which textural feature in high-grade metamorphic rocks?
options: Alignment of platy mica minerals along parallel planes
Alternating light (felsic) and dark (mafic) mineral layers
Random orientation of mineral grains without any layering
Lineation defined by elongate minerals parallel to the fold axis
questions.solution: Gneiss: high grade. Segregation into bands. Compositional layering.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which statement about the Moho is correct?
options: It separates the outer core from the mantle and generates the geomagnetic field
It separates the crust from the mantle and shows a velocity increase
It lies within the crust at the depth where temperature exceeds the Curie point
It is a boundary inside the mantle across which seismic velocity drops
questions.solution: The Mohorovičić discontinuity marks the crust–mantle boundary, where P-wave velocity jumps.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Banded iron formations, the main source of iron ore, are characterized by which features and types?
options: Phanerozoic in age, being restricted largely to the Mesozoic coal-bearing basins of Gondwana
Cretaceous in age, formed in shallow Cretaceous epicontinental seas
Tertiary in age, linked to Cenozoic uplift and laterite development
Main Fe ore. Hematite + magnetite. Precambrian. Superior and Algoma types
questions.solution: BIF: iron precipitated from seawater. Oxygenation by cyanobacteria. Major Fe reserve.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A dipping coal seam outcrops over a horizontal width of 100 m on flat ground and dips at 35°. Its true thickness is about:
questions.solution: True thickness = horizontal width × sin(dip) = 100×sin35° ≈ 57.36 m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The general three-dimensional groundwater flow equation reduces to Laplace's equation under which condition?
options: Darcy's law applied only to horizontal flow, with no variation in head or velocity across space
∂/∂x(K_x·∂h/∂x) + ∂/∂y(K_y·∂h/∂y) + ∂/∂z(K_z·∂h/∂z) = S_s·∂h/∂t. Laplace: steady
Steady state conditions require that the storage term in the groundwater flow equation be zero
Transient groundwater flow ignores the storage term and assumes a constant hydraulic conductivity everywhere
questions.solution: Steady: ∂²h/∂x² + ∂²h/∂y² + ∂²h/∂z² = 0 (Laplace). Transient: diffusion equation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Tilted trees, displaced walls and bent fence posts are commonly cited field evidence for which slow mass-wasting process?
options: Tilted trees (pistol-butt), displaced walls, bent fence posts
Lateral shifting of a river channel across its floodplain over time
Curved scars left by rapid downslope movement of material
Deepening of a river bed by vertical downcutting
questions.solution: Creep: slow downslope movement. Indicators: tilted trees, curved soil profiles, displaced objects.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What determines whether a rock can be ripped or must be blasted?
options: Seismic velocity (Vp) determines ripping vs blasting. Vp < 1500 m/s: easy rip
Rippability depends only on the density of the intact rock material and nothing else
All rocks above Vp of 3000 m/s can still be ripped by heavy dozers
Grain size alone decides whether ripping or blasting is required
questions.solution: Rippability: Caterpillar chart. Vp (m/s): easy <1500, marginal 1500-2000, hard >2000 → blast.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the age, basin setting, and characteristic fossil content of the Siwalik Group?
options: Marine fossils of open-ocean foraminifera deposited in a deep-water shelf setting
Miocene-Pleistocene. Himalayan foreland basin. Fossils: mammals (elephant, horse, ape)
Only volcanic rocks with thick andesitic lava flows and tuff horizons throughout the section
No fossils of any kind due to complete oxidation of the original organic material
questions.solution: Siwalik: sandstone, conglomerate. Himalayan uplift record. Ramapithecus, Sivapithecus.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A P-wave travels at 8 km/s and arrives 10 s after the earthquake. The (approx.) distance to the source is:
options: 80 km
40 km
10 km
0.8 km
questions.solution: distance = velocity × time = 8×10 = 80 km.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer (K = 10 m/day) of cross-section 100 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.02. The groundwater discharge is about:
options: 1000 m³/day
20 m³/day
10 m³/day
40 m³/day

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the active layer above permafrost, and on what does its depth depend?
options: A permanently frozen zone that never thaws even during the warm summer months of the year
The frozen crust that lies below the permafrost table at depth
A zone of deep thaw that remains unfrozen throughout the year
Seasonal thaw layer above permafrost. Depth: 0.5-5m depending on climate
questions.solution: Active layer: thaws in summer, refreezes in winter. Frost heave. Pile foundations for structures.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Exfoliation (sheeting) joints are curved fractures parallel to the topographic surface that form mainly due to which process?
options: Planar joints formed by regional tectonic compression in massive bedrock
Horizontal joints in sedimentary beds produced during lithification and dewatering
Vertical cooling joints in basaltic lava flows formed during contraction
Curved joints parallel to topographic surface. Unloading (erosion)
questions.solution: Exfoliation: formation of sheet joints. Onion-like weathering. Granite domes (Half Dome).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which regions of the electromagnetic spectrum, from visible through near-infrared to microwave, are used in remote sensing?
options: Only the visible and near-infrared portions of the spectrum
Only thermal infrared, used for temperature measurement
Visible (0.4-0.7 μm), NIR, SWIR, TIR, Microwave (radar)
Only microwave, which cannot sense optical properties
questions.solution: Multispectral: multiple bands. Hyperspectral: hundreds of narrow bands.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In fold classification, what are the key geometric elements (hinge, limb, axial plane, plunge) that define an anticline or syncline?
options: Anticline is a downfold and syncline is an upfold, named by their relative depth
Anticline (upfold), Syncline (downfold). Hinge, limb, axial plane, plunge
Both fold types are geometrically identical and differ only in their orientation
Folds are classified solely by their wavelength and never by their shape or age
questions.solution: Anticline: oldest in core. Syncline: youngest in core.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Thermal infrared remote sensing measures:
options: Surface temperature and emissivity
Vegetation health through chlorophyll content
Soil moisture in the root zone directly
Water depth through penetration of the column
questions.solution: TIR: 8-14 um wavelength. Detects emitted thermal radiation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes solifluction and the alternative name by which the process is known?
options: Rapid free fall of rock fragments from a steep cliff face to the base of the slope
Fast-moving flow of water-saturated material down a steep slope in a short time
Downslope movement of dry granular material under the influence of gravity with no water involved
Slow downslope flow of water-saturated soil over permafrost. Gelifluction
questions.solution: Solifluction: lobes, sheets. 1-10 cm/yr. Gelifluction: thaw of ice lenses. Terrace-like landforms.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: From a digital elevation model, how are slope and aspect each defined in terms of elevation change?
options: Slope = max rate of change. Aspect = direction of max slope (0-360°)
Slope is the elevation value; aspect is the total relief of the area
Aspect is expressed in metres above mean sea level
Both are derived from land cover, not from elevation
questions.solution: Slope: degrees or %. Derived from DEM (3×3 window, e.g., Horn algorithm). Aspect: N, S, E, W.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which statement about mining method selection is correct?
options: A high stripping ratio favours opencast mining of the shallow seam
A high stripping ratio favours underground over opencast mining
Deep seams are always worked by opencast extraction methods
Stripping ratio has no bearing on the method of selection at all
questions.solution: When too much overburden must be removed per tonne (high stripping ratio), underground mining is preferred.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An opencast block of 10000 m² has 30 m of overburden above the seam. The overburden volume to be removed is:
options: 0.2 million m³
0.3 million m³
0.6 million m³
0 million m³
questions.solution: Volume = area × depth = 10000×30 = 300000 m³ = 0.3 million m³.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which liquid is commonly used in heavy mineral separation for provenance studies?
options: Bromoform (SG=2.89) separates light from heavy minerals
Magnetic separation using a Frantz isodynamic separator
Optical sorting of grains under plane-polarized light
Chemical dissolution followed by gravimetric measurement
questions.solution: Heavy minerals: SG>2.89. Zircon, tourmaline, rutile (ultra-stable). Garnet, staurolite, kyanite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Cooper-Jacob straight-line method: drawdown s vs log(t) plot slope:
options: Slope = 2.3Q/T measured over one log cycle
Slope = Q/T for the early part of the data
Slope = Q/(2πT) for the steady state of flow
Slope = 2.3Q/(4πT) for late-time data
questions.solution: Cooper-Jacob: valid for small u (<0.01). Slope Δs over one log cycle = 2.3Q/(4πT).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 20% volatile matter and 8% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (4+20+8) = 68%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a strike-slip fault, displacement is horizontal; what distinguishes a left-lateral fault from a right-lateral fault?
options: Horizontal displacement. Left-lateral vs right-lateral
Vertical displacement where the hanging wall drops down relative to the footwall
Oblique slip with equal horizontal and vertical displacement components
Rotation of blocks about a vertical axis without any horizontal translation
questions.solution: Strike-slip: San Andreas Fault. Transform plate boundary.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Garnet, a common metamorphic mineral, belongs to which crystal system?
options: Hexagonal system
Triclinic system
Cubic (isometric)
Tetragonal system
questions.solution: Garnet: dodecahedral or trapezohedral crystals. Used as abrasive.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer (K = 10 m/day) of cross-section 500 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.01. The groundwater discharge is about:
options: 5000 m³/day
100 m³/day
50 m³/day
25 m³/day

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly represents the general chemical formula of the mineral tourmaline?
options: (Ca,K,Na,□)(Li,Mg,Fe²⁺,Mn²⁺,Al)₃(Al,Cr,Fe³⁺,V)₆(BO₃)₃Si₆O₁₈(OH)₄
Ca₅(PO₄)₃(F,OH,Cl) — calcium phosphate with fluorine
K(Mg,Fe)₃AlSi₃O₁₀(OH)₂ — hydrous aluminosilicate of the mica group
Mg₃(Si₄O₁₀)(OH)₂ — hydrated magnesium sheet silicate
questions.solution: Tourmaline: complex borosilicate. Wide solid solution. Schorl (Fe), elbaite (Li,Na), dravite (Mg).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: P-T path determination from garnet zoning and inclusions:
options: Garnet core = early P-T. Rim = peak conditions. Inclusions record path
Garnet rims record the earliest conditions of metamorphism
Inclusions are younger than the host garnet and record late events
Only the bulk composition of the whole rock is ever required for the analysis
questions.solution: Garnet: chronometer. Inclusion assemblages at different distances from core = different P-T. Thermobarometry.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: When a competent layer is stretched between incompetent rocks during deformation, what is the resulting pinch-and-swell structure called?
options: Pinch-and-swell structure formed in an incompetent layer squeezed between competent beds
Fold structure produced by vertical buckling of alternating competent and incompetent strata
Boudin (barrel-shaped) structure in competent layer stretched in incompetent matrix
A type of unconformity formed where competent beds are truncated by erosion at the surface
questions.solution: Boudinage: competent layer (quartzite) boudins in incompetent matrix (schist). Necking.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 20% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (4+20+15) = 61%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To which structural group of silicate minerals does biotite belong?
options: Tectosilicates (framework silicate minerals)
Inosilicates (chain silicate mineral group)
Phyllosilicates (sheet silicates — micas)
Cyclosilicates (ring silicate mineral group)
questions.solution: Biotite — black mica. One perfect basal cleavage. Common in granite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In GIS-based hydrological modeling, what processing of a DEM is required to derive flow accumulation, stream networks, and watersheds?
options: Flow accumulation and watershed delineation can be run on an unfilled DEM directly
Stream network extraction requires only slope; sink filling is optional preprocessing
Flow accumulation, stream network, watershed delineation. Sink filling required
Watershed boundaries are derived from aspect alone, without flow direction grids
questions.solution: DEM → fill sinks → flow direction (D8) → flow accumulation → stream threshold → watershed.

questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 8% moisture, 30% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (8+30+15) = 47%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Mylonite, a foliated rock from ductile shear zones, forms chiefly by which process?
options: Coarse-grained rock formed by static recrystallization under heat alone without deformation
Brecciated rock containing angular clasts produced by brittle faulting without any subsequent recrystallization or melting
Impact melt glass formed by frictional heating during a large meteorite impact event
Fine-grained, foliated rock in ductile shear zone. Grain size reduction by dynamic recrystallization
questions.solution: Mylonite: ductile deformation. Porphyroclasts in fine matrix. S-C fabrics. Protomylonite→mylonite→ultramylonite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An opencast block of 10000 m² has 50 m of overburden above the seam. The overburden volume to be removed is:
options: 0.3 million m³
0 million m³
0.5 million m³
1 million m³
questions.solution: Volume = area × depth = 10000×50 = 500000 m³ = 0.5 million m³.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To extract 5 m³ of coal, 45 m³ of overburden must be removed. The stripping ratio is:
questions.solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 45/5 = 9 : 1.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a fluvial meandering facies model, channel and floodplain deposits together produce a vertical profile that shows what trend?
options: Alluvial fan with debris flows, sheetfloods and sieve deposits at the mountain front, fining basinward
Delta with mouth bars, distributary channels and prodelta muds
Channel (lag + lateral accretion) + floodplain (levee + crevasse splay + swamp). Vertically fining
Braided alluvium with stacked gravel sheets and minor overbank fines
questions.solution: Meandering: point bar (epsilon cross-bedding). Lateral accretion surfaces (LAS). Mud plug.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer has hydraulic conductivity 50 m/day and a hydraulic gradient of 0.05. The Darcy velocity is:
options: 2.5 m/day
5 m/day
50 m/day
1000 m/day

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which option correctly describes a barrier island, its lagoon and the inlets that cut through it?
options: Island of resistant bedrock rising steeply above the sea surface offshore from the coast
Island built by volcanic eruptions on the sea floor near the coastline of the mainland
Long, narrow sand island parallel to coast. Lagoon behind. Inlet cuts
Sand ridge attached to the mainland coast at one of its two ends
questions.solution: Barrier: wave-dominated. Dune ridge, beach, washover fans. Sea-level rise → barrier transgression.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Foliation (planar fabric) is a feature of which rock type?
options: All igneous rocks without exception
All sedimentary rocks
Many metamorphic rocks
Only volcanic tuffs
questions.solution: Directed pressure aligns minerals into foliation in metamorphic rocks like schist and gneiss.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the approximate specific gravity value of the common mineral quartz?
questions.solution: Quartz SG ~2.65. Heavy minerals have SG > 2.85.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A buried erosion surface separating older from much younger rocks is a(n):
options: Plane of maximum curvature along the crest of an anticlinal fold
Unconformity
Surface of continuous deposition with no gap in the geologic record
Fracture along which displacement has occurred between the two blocks
questions.solution: An unconformity represents a gap (missing time) in the rock record.
